title: Macaulay2 LSP Index
description: Schema for ONE LINE of m2-index.jsonl, the combined reference the Macaulay2 LSP consumes (compressed typecheck corpus + per-object hover markdown). The file is JSONL: one JSON object per line, no array wrapper or comment header. The first line is a MetaRecord; every other line is a CompiledObject. Validate each line against this schema. Generated from the Markdown docs by scripts/assemble_jsonl.m2; do not edit by hand.

MetaRecord.description: The first line of the file. Carries the default-loaded package baseline: the packages M2 loads on a fresh `-q` start (Core plus its transitive dependencies), i.e. those usable without an explicit needsPackage. This is the LSP's 'in scope without import' baseline.

RefKey.description: A cross-reference to another object: a `$Package$Name` key (e.g. `$Core$ZZ`) once the target's home package is known, or a bare normalized name (no `$` prefix) when the target is not present in any extracted package. The leading `$` is deliberately invalid as an M2 identifier, so a reference key never collides with a real symbol name.

CompiledObject.description: One documented object. Identity/resolution fields are present on every entry; the callable, operator, and type field groups appear only for the relevant kind. An absent field means not-applicable -- the corpus emits no empty placeholders.

kind.description: Object category. Drives which optional field groups are present.

package.description: Home package, as a reference to the package object (e.g. `$Core$Core`). With normalized_name this also disambiguates resolution across packages, mirroring M2's loaded-package scoping -- take refName to recover the bare package name (e.g. "Core").

class.description: Runtime class, as a reference to the type object (e.g. `$Core$MethodFunctionWithOptions`).

aliases.description: Other names that resolve to this object.

extra_keys.description: Additional documentation lookup keys that resolve here.

typical_value.description: Function-level return type: a LOWER BOUND on the result type (the result is an instance of it or a subtype), possibly recovered from documentation. The per-method typicalValue is usually more precise. null when unknown. [callables]

methods.description: Callable signatures. For method functions and operators these are per-domain M2 installations; for a non-overloadable plain function an entry is a static signature, not an M2 method installation. [callables]

markdown.description: Rendered hover documentation for this object (real `#` headings). Omitted when the object is undocumented -- absence means no hover, matching the corpus's 'absent = not applicable' convention.

protected.description: Whether the exported symbol is protected from reassignment; null when unknown.

mutable.description: Result of isMutable on the exported value, independently of symbol protection; null when unknown. For a type this describes the type object itself, not its instances.

source.description: Source lines covering the definition span when the source file is readable; null otherwise.

CompiledMethod.description: A callable signature: an ordered input domain and its return type. It is an M2 installation for a method function or operator, but only a static signature for a non-overloadable plain function. The core of type checking -- resolve a call's argument types against `domain` (walking each argument's class->parent chain), and take `typicalValue` as the result.

domain.description: Input types in order; [] for a 0-ary or operator form.

typicalValue.description: Return type, or null if unknown. Bounded by `exact`.

exact.description: true: typicalValue is the EXACT return type. false (default): a LOWER BOUND -- the result is an instance of it or some subtype, so a checker must accept any subtype.

returnInherited.description: Present and true when typicalValue was inherited from the function's documented return type (M2 did not type this overload), so it is less certain than an M2-provided per-method type. Absent otherwise.

source.description: Source lines covering the definition span when the source file is readable; null otherwise.

CompiledOption.description: A keyword option. The human-readable option description is dropped from the typecheck corpus.

default.description: Default value, as a string; null when none is recorded.

valueType.description: Accepted value type, when known; null otherwise.

possibleValues.description: Enumerated accepted values, when known; [] otherwise.

OperatorInfo.description: Syntactic shape of an operator. Read arity follows from the form: binary = 2 operands, prefix/postfix = 1. The per-domain read installations live in the object's `methods` array; the assignment form's installations are in `assignment` here.

forms.description: Syntactic forms the operator supports. "binary"/"prefix"/"postfix" are read forms (from M2's operatorAttributes); "assignment" is the `x op y = z` form, present only when a genuine typed assignment installation exists (see `assignment`).

attributes.description: Per-form attribute lists. The only attribute M2 exposes is "Flexible" (the form accepts user-installed methods).

assignment.description: Typed installations of the assignment form `x op y = z`, surfaced by M2's `methods(symbol =)` under the (op,=) key. Only genuine operations are kept -- those with a concrete operand -- not the blanket (Type,Type)/(Thing,Thing) handlers M2 installs for every flexible operator. Present only when non-empty; mostly subscript assignment (op "_"). No value/return type is recorded (M2 exposes none).

domain.description: Operand types in order (the left/right of the operator), as reference keys; the assigned value's type is not part of the signature.

filename.description: Absolute filename on the extraction machine.

SourceLocation.description: Definition span returned by Macaulay2 locate. Rows are one-based; columns are zero-based; the stop position is exclusive.
